claims.statement: Each Open-Inspect session id maps 1:1 to a SessionDO Durable Object (env.SESSION.idFromName(sessionId)); the DO owns the session's authoritative aggregate in an embedded SQLite database (ctx.storage.sql), while the global D1 session index is a listing/query mirror projected from the DO.

A session targets exactly one of four mutually exclusive modes: a single repository (scalar repoOwner+repoName), an ordered ad-hoc multi-repository list (up to 10), a saved environment (environmentId), or no repository; createSessionRequestSchema's hasExclusiveSessionTarget enforces that at most one mode is present.

MAX_TARGET_REPOSITORIES = 10 bounds session and environment member lists; sessionRepositoriesInputSchema rejects empty lists, duplicate owner/name pairs, and duplicate repoName across owners because checkout paths are /workspace/{repoName}.

In multi-repo sessions the first repository is the primary: it is mirrored into the scalar repo_owner/repo_name/base_branch columns in both stores (row-0-mirrors-scalars invariant), drives session-scoped settings and secret precedence, and initializeSession plus /internal/init both reject a repositories[0] that does not identity- and branch-equal the scalar mirror.

Repository context is a triple invariant: repoOwner, repoName, and repoId must be present together or all absent; no-repo sessions must not carry repoId, baseBranch, or any branch context. It is enforced by the DO session-table CHECK constraint, upsertSession, and initializeSession before any write.

A repo owner may contain / (GitLab subgroups); only repo_name is a single path segment. parseRepositoryFullName splits on the last slash, and all repo-identity comparisons are case-insensitive (repoIdentityEquals / normalizeOptionalRepositoryPair).

In multi-repo sessions each repository is cloned into its own /workspace/{repoName} directory; intermediate steps run per repository in position order, and pushes/PRs are per-repository — one session can produce PRs in several repositories, and the sidebar lists every member with its branch and PR.

initializeSession writes the D1 index first and initializes the DO second — an invariant so failures are caught before any sandbox is spawned; if the DO init then fails or times out, markSessionFailed compensates the D1 row to 'failed' so it never lists as a phantom 'created' session.

The DO-side /internal/init handler writes the entire initial aggregate — session row, ordered member repository set, pending sandbox row (status pending, git_sync_status pending), and the owner participant — in one synchronous transaction, then schedules the warm sandbox spawn.

SessionStatus and SandboxStatus describe different levels: SessionStatus ('created','active','completed','failed','archived','cancelled') is the durable conversation lifecycle independent of compute, while SandboxStatus ('pending','spawning','connecting','warming','ready','stale','snapshotting','stopped','failed') describes only the current sandbox incarnation; a session may be completed with a live sandbox or active with none, and the two vocabularies must never be conflated.

The DO session table is a singleton row (id = DO id) carrying the scalar repo mirror, opencode_session_id, model, reasoning_effort, status, parent_session_id, spawn_source, spawn_depth, code_server_enabled, vnc_enabled, total_cost, sandbox_settings JSON, environment_id provenance, and timestamps, with a CHECK that no-repo rows have no repo_id or base_branch.

created becomes active when the first prompt is enqueued (never at creation); after an execution the status settles to active when prompts remain queued, otherwise completed/failed by outcome; settleFromMessageState derives the idle status from the latest terminal message and deliberately falls back to 'created' for a session with no messages at all so the abandoned-draft sweep can reclaim it.

SessionStatusService is the single place every status transition fans out to its three projections — connected clients (broadcast), the D1 session index (status plus terminal metrics mirror), and the parent session's DO (child rollup) — and every public method is a transition on that one noun.

D1 session status updates are monotonic: updateStatus applies only updated_at values greater than or equal to the stored one, protecting against out-of-order async writes, and repairIndexStatus re-projects a stale D1 mirror to the DO's current status without claiming new activity.

Cancellation atomically closes the local aggregate before publishing: the callback terminalizes unfinished messages synchronously so no request can observe cancelled status with unfinished messages or accept work between the two mutations.

Archive requires a participant caller and rejects sessions with queued work (409) and cancelled sessions; unarchive is restoring, not starting — it settles the status from what the messages imply rather than asserting 'active'.

Warm sessions never prompted are retired by the abandoned-draft sweep (ABANDONED_DRAFT_TTL_MS = 8h, cron '23 * * * *', capped at 50 per tick): the D1 index selects created rows older than the TTL and asks each DO via /internal/expire-draft; a 404 lets the index retire the orphan row directly, and a session that moved on gets its stale index status repaired.

The shared predicates over SessionStatus are named for their questions: isSessionPromptable excludes only archived/cancelled; isTurnSettled (completed/failed/cancelled) governs metric sync and deliberately excludes archived; isSessionInactive (completed/failed/archived/cancelled) answers child-accounting and cancellability questions.

Participants are the session's membership and security boundary: the creator becomes the owner participant (role 'owner'), later joiners are 'member'; SCM credentials are stored AES-GCM-encrypted per participant, the WebSocket auth token is stored as a SHA-256 hash, and participant membership gates archive/unarchive and WebSocket subscription.

Messages are both the prompt queue and history: at most one message may be 'processing' at a time (unique partial index), enqueueing a pending message transitions the session to active in the same DO turn, and messages carry idempotency keys (client_request_id, request_fingerprint) plus autofix feedback/PR keys.

Events are the append-only agent timeline (tool calls, tokens, errors, git sync) with a monotonically assigned unique timeline_sequence for cursor paging; token and execution_complete events upsert by stable composite ids so re-delivery never duplicates.

Artifacts (pr, screenshot, video, preview, branch) carry typed JSON metadata; PR artifacts are a live view of the D1 session_pull_requests record, and PR artifacts written before multi-repo support carry no repo identity and by construction belong to the session's primary.

Lineage is recorded as parent_session_id, spawn_source ('user','agent','automation','github-bot','linear-bot','slack-bot'), and spawn_depth (0 for top-level); the D1 insert computes root_session_id as the parent's root when a parent_session_id is present, else the session itself.

Child spawning is prompt-driven and scalar in v1: /internal/spawn-context requires a processing message to resolve the prompt author and children inherit only the parent's primary repository (even for multi-repo parents); MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH = 2 and per-parent maxConcurrent/maxTotal child caps from resolved sandbox settings bound the tree.

Children inherit their parent's settings scope (primary repo plus environment overrides) and copy the parent's pinned managed-skill manifest (skillManifestSourceSessionId); child status/title changes notify the parent DO via /internal/child-session-update so its clients refresh in real time.

SessionIndexStore.create batches the session row, ordered member rows, the resolved pinned skill manifest (or a verbatim copy of a parent's), and the complete immutable model-provider-auth snapshot into one D1 batch, so a partially initialized session can never appear in listings; the insert throws if the session row insert is skipped.

Session list queries match a repository filter through the session_repositories membership table so a session is found through ANY member, with the scalar arm as the pre-feature fallback; excludeAutomationLineage backs the 'Mine' view by excluding automation runs and bot-initiated github-bot sessions; pages order by updated_at DESC and attach ordered members, PR summaries, and viewer read state via attachSessionListMetadata.

The session inbox is a lineage-aware read model with categories needs_attention/in_progress/finished: a recursive CTE groups each root session with its descendant sessions into SessionInboxItem, ranked by the lineage's latest activity, with cursors keyed on (latest_updated_at, root_session_id).

Per-user read state is derived from the D1 sessions.latest_terminal_message_id column against session_read_states rows, so the unread badge works off the index mirror; the DO records the latest terminal message monotonic-guarded via recordLatestTerminalMessage.

Environment-launched sessions snapshot the environment's members at creation (resolveEnvironmentTarget feeds resolveSessionRepositories) and record sessions.environment_id as provenance, which is FK-less and benignly dangling after the environment is deleted; session-target secrets then come from global + environment only, never member repos.

Session repository lists are resolved all-or-nothing against the SCM provider (resolveSessionRepositories): a session boots one sandbox for the whole set, so a single unresolvable member fails the create, naming every failing repository and raising 400 for clean no-access or 500 for provider errors.

Session identity is read through the scalar mirror with a synthesized one-entry member list for pre-multi-repo sessions: buildSessionRepositories returns the stored session_repositories rows in position order, or a one-entry list built from the scalar columns when no rows exist; per-repo git state (branch_name, base_sha, current_sha) is written by push handling onto the member rows.

A session is addressed publicly by its session_name when it has one, else its row id, else the Durable Object id; the latched resolver freezes on the first row-backed id because session_name is immutable after init.

All internal DO routes (init, state, prompt, stop, archive, expire-draft, spawn-context, child-session-update, etc.) are constants in SessionInternalPaths imported by both the router-side runtime client and the DO route table, so the two sides cannot drift on path strings.

Per-session feature flags (code_server_enabled, vnc_enabled) and the sandbox_settings JSON blob are resolved at creation from the primary member plus environment overrides and persisted on the session row; D1 mirrors total_cost, active_duration_ms (sum over completed messages), message_count, and pr_count via updateMetrics.
